title.zh: 卷四 本紀第四 簡文帝
title.raw: 卷四 本紀第四 簡文帝 Volume 4: Emperor Jianwen

sentences.zh: 梁書卷第四 本紀第四

translations.literal: Book of Liang, Volume 4, Basic Annals 4
translations.idiomatic: Book of Liang, Volume 4, Annals 4

sentences.zh: 簡文帝

translations.literal: Emperor Jianwen
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Jianwen

sentences.zh: 太宗簡文皇帝諱綱，字世纘，小字六通，高祖第三子，昭明太子母弟也。

translations.literal: The Taizong Emperor Jianwen was tabooed Gang, style name Shizuan, childhood name Liutong; he was the third son of the Gaozu and a uterine younger brother of Crown Prince Zhaoming.
translations.idiomatic: Taizong Emperor Jianwen, personal name Gang, courtesy name Shizuan, childhood name Liutong, was Gaozu's third son and Zhaoming Crown Prince's younger brother by the same mother.

sentences.zh: 天監二年十月丁未，生於顯陽殿。

translations.literal: In the tenth month, day dingwei, year 2 of Tianjian, he was born in Xianyang Hall.
translations.idiomatic: On dingwei in the tenth month of Tianjian 2 he was born in Xianyang Hall.

sentences.zh: 五年，封晉安王，食邑八千戶。

translations.literal: In year 5 he was enfeoffed as Prince of Jin'an with a fief of eight thousand households.
translations.idiomatic: In year 5 he was made Prince of Jin'an with a fief of eight thousand households.

sentences.zh: 八年，為雲麾將軍，領石頭戍軍事，量置佐吏。

translations.literal: In year 8 he was made General of the Cloud Banner, supervising military affairs at the Shitou garrison, with assistant officials appointed as needed.
translations.idiomatic: In year 8 he became General of the Cloud Banner, took charge of Shitou garrison affairs, and had aides appointed as required.

sentences.zh: 九年，遷使持節、都督南北兗青徐冀五州諸軍事、宣毅將軍、南兗州刺史。

translations.literal: In year 9 he was transferred to Bearer of the Staff, Commander over military affairs in the five provinces North and South Yan, Qing, Xu, and Ji, made General Who Proclaims Resolution and South Yanzhou Inspector.
translations.idiomatic: In year 9 he was made Bearer of the Staff and commander of the five Yan, Qing, Xu, and Ji provinces, General Who Proclaims Resolution, and South Yanzhou inspector.

sentences.zh: 十二年，入為宣惠將軍、丹陽尹。

translations.literal: In year 12 he entered the capital as General Who Proclaims Grace and Intendant of Danyang.
translations.idiomatic: In year 12 he entered court as General Who Proclaims Grace and intendant of Danyang.

sentences.zh: 十三年，出為使持節、都督荊雍梁南北秦益寧七州諸軍事、南蠻校尉、荊州刺史，將軍如故。

translations.literal: In year 13 he went out as Bearer of the Staff, Commander over military affairs in the seven provinces Jing, Yong, Liang, North and South Qin, Yi, and Ning, made Colonel of the Southern Barbarians and Jingzhou Inspector, his generalship unchanged.
translations.idiomatic: In year 13 he went out as Bearer of the Staff, commander of Jing, Yong, Liang, the two Qin, Yi, and Ning, Colonel of the Southern Barbarians, and Jingzhou inspector, retaining his generalship.

sentences.zh: 十四年，徙為都督江州諸軍事、雲麾將軍、江州刺史，持節如故。

translations.literal: In year 14 he was reassigned as Commander over military affairs in Jiangzhou, General of the Cloud Banner and Jiangzhou Inspector, Bearer of the Staff unchanged.
translations.idiomatic: In year 14 he was reassigned commander of Jiangzhou, General of the Cloud Banner, and Jiangzhou inspector, still Bearer of the Staff.

sentences.zh: 十七年，徵為西中郎將、領石頭戍軍事，尋復為宣惠將軍、丹陽尹，加侍中。

translations.literal: In year 17 he was summoned as Leader of the Palace Gentlemen of the West, supervising the Shitou garrison; soon restored as General Who Proclaims Grace and Intendant of Danyang, additionally made Palace Attendant.
translations.idiomatic: In year 17 he was recalled as Leader of the Palace Gentlemen of the West with Shitou garrison duties, then again General Who Proclaims Grace and Danyang intendant, with Palace Attendant added.

sentences.zh: 普通元年，出為使持節、都督益寧雍梁南北秦沙七州諸軍事、益州刺史；

translations.literal: In year 1 of Putong he went out as Bearer of the Staff, Commander over military affairs in the seven provinces Yi, Ning, Yong, Liang, North and South Qin, and Sha, and made Yi Province Inspector;
translations.idiomatic: In Putong 1 he went out as Bearer of the Staff, commander of Yi, Ning, Yong, Liang, the two Qin, and Sha, and Yi province inspector;

sentences.zh: 未拜，改授雲麾將軍、南徐州刺史。

translations.literal: before assuming the post, he was reassigned as General of the Cloud Banner and South Xuzhou Inspector.
translations.idiomatic: before taking office he was reassigned General of the Cloud Banner and South Xuzhou inspector.

sentences.zh: 四年，徙為使持節、都督雍梁、南北秦四州郢州之竟陵司州之隨郡諸軍事，平西將軍、寧蠻校尉、雍州刺史。

translations.literal: In year 4 he was reassigned as Bearer of the Staff, Commander over military affairs in Yong and Liang, North and South Qin, the four provinces, Jingzhou's Jingling, and Sizhou's Su commandery, made General Who Pacifies the West, Colonel of Pacified Barbarians, and Yongzhou Inspector.
translations.idiomatic: In year 4 he was reassigned Bearer of the Staff, commander of Yong, Liang, the two Qin, and related districts, General Who Pacifies the West, Colonel of Pacified Barbarians, and Yongzhou inspector.

sentences.zh: 五年，進號安北將軍。

translations.literal: In year 5 he was advanced to General Who Pacifies the North.
translations.idiomatic: In year 5 he was promoted to General Who Pacifies the North.

sentences.zh: 七年，權進都督荊、益、南梁三州諸軍事。

translations.literal: In year 7 he was provisionally advanced as Commander over military affairs in Jing, Yi, and South Liang.
translations.idiomatic: In year 7 he was provisionally made commander of Jing, Yi, and South Liang.

sentences.zh: 是歲，丁所生穆貴嬪喪，上表陳解，詔還攝本任。

translations.literal: That year, on mourning for his birth mother Honored Consort Mu, he submitted a memorial requesting release; an edict ordered him to resume his original duties.
translations.idiomatic: That year, when his birth mother Honored Consort Mu died, he asked to resign but was ordered back to his post.

sentences.zh: 中大通元年，詔依先給鼓吹一部。

translations.literal: In year 1 of Zhongdatong an edict granted him one suite of drums and pipes as before.
translations.idiomatic: In Zhongdatong 1 an edict granted him the usual suite of drums and pipes.

sentences.zh: 二年，徵為都督南揚、徐二州諸軍事、驃騎將軍、揚州刺史。

translations.literal: In year 2 he was summoned as Commander over military affairs in South Yang and Xu, made General of Agile Cavalry and Yangzhou Inspector.
translations.idiomatic: In year 2 he was recalled as commander of South Yang and Xu, General of Agile Cavalry, and Yangzhou inspector.

sentences.zh: 三年四月乙巳，昭明太子薨。

translations.literal: In the fourth month, day yisi, year 3, Crown Prince Zhaoming died.
translations.idiomatic: On yisi in the fourth month of year 3 Crown Prince Zhaoming died.

sentences.zh: 五月丙申，詔曰：「非至公無以主天下，非博愛無以臨四海。

translations.literal: In the fifth month, day bingshen, an edict said: "Without utmost fairness one cannot rule all under Heaven; without universal love one cannot oversee the four seas.
translations.idiomatic: On bingshen in the fifth month an edict said, "Without utmost fairness one cannot hold the realm; without universal love one cannot govern the four seas.

sentences.zh: 所以堯舜克讓，惟德是與；

translations.literal: Therefore Yao and Shun could yield, bestowing office only on virtue;
translations.idiomatic: Therefore Yao and Shun yielded the throne, giving it only to the virtuous;

sentences.zh: 文王舍伯邑考而立武王，格于上下，光于四表。

translations.literal: King Wen set aside Bo Yi Kao and established King Wu, reaching above and below, shining to the four quarters.
translations.idiomatic: King Wen passed over Bo Yi Kao and installed King Wu, harmonizing above and below and shining across the four quarters.

sentences.zh: 今岱宗牢落，天步艱難，淳風猶鬱，黎民未乂，自非克明克哲，允武允文，豈能荷神器之重，嗣龍圖之尊。

translations.literal: Now Mount Tai stands desolate and the heavenly course is hard; pure custom still is troubled and the people are not settled—unless one is bright and wise, truly martial and cultured, how could one bear the weight of the sacred vessel and inherit the dragon throne?
translations.idiomatic: Now the sacred mountain is empty and the heavenly steps are hard; pure custom is still troubled and the people unrested—without brightness, wisdom, martial merit, and culture, who could bear the sacred regalia and succeed to the dragon throne?

sentences.zh: 晉安王綱，文義生知，孝敬自然，威惠外宣，德行內敏，羣后歸美，率土宅心。

translations.literal: Prince of Jin'an Gang, gifted in letters and right by nature, filial and respectful by instinct, his authority and kindness proclaimed abroad and virtue and conduct keen within, the feudal lords admired him and all the land took him to heart.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Gang of Jin'an was gifted in letters and principles, naturally filial and respectful, his authority and kindness known abroad and his virtue keen within; the lords praised him and the realm took him to heart.

sentences.zh: 可立為皇太子。

translations.literal: He may be established as crown prince.
translations.idiomatic: He is to be established as crown prince.

sentences.zh: 」七月乙亥，臨軒策拜，以脩繕東宮，權居東府。

translations.literal: On yihai in the seventh month, the enthronement ceremony was held at the imperial hall; because the Eastern Palace was under repair, he temporarily resided at the Eastern Mansion.
translations.idiomatic: On yihai in the seventh month he was invested at the throne hall; while the Eastern Palace was repaired he lodged temporarily at the Eastern Mansion.

sentences.zh: 四年九月，移還東宮。

translations.literal: In the ninth month of year 4 he moved back to the Eastern Palace.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth month of year 4 he returned to the Eastern Palace.

sentences.zh: 太清三年五月丙辰，高祖崩。

translations.literal: In the fifth month, day bingchen, year 3 of Taiqing, the Gaozu died.
translations.idiomatic: On bingchen in the fifth month of Taiqing 3 Gaozu died.

sentences.zh: 辛巳，卽皇帝位。

translations.literal: On xinsi he ascended the imperial throne.
translations.idiomatic: On xinsi he took the throne.

sentences.zh: 詔曰：「朕以不造，夙丁閔凶。

translations.literal: An edict said: "Our lack of fortune afflicts us; from early we suffered this calamity.
translations.idiomatic: An edict said, "Ill-fated as I am, I have long borne this grief.

sentences.zh: 大行皇帝奄棄萬國，攀慕號躃，厝身靡所。

translations.literal: The late emperor suddenly abandoned the myriad realms; we cling and wail and have nowhere to place ourselves.
translations.idiomatic: The late emperor has suddenly left the myriad realms; in longing and wailing I have nowhere to set myself.

sentences.zh: 猥以寡德，越居民上，煢煢在疚，罔知所託，方賴籓輔，社稷用安。

translations.literal: Unworthily with slight virtue we have crossed above the people; alone in anguish we know not where to lean, yet rely on the feudal helpers that the altars may be secure.
translations.idiomatic: With slight virtue I have undeservedly risen above the people; alone in grief I know not whom to trust, and must rely on the feudatories to keep the altars secure.

sentences.zh: 謹遵先旨，顧命遺澤，宜加億兆。

translations.literal: Respectfully following the prior will and the bequeathed grace of the final charge, benefit should be added for the hundred millions.
translations.idiomatic: Respectfully following the prior command and the grace of the deathbed charge, the hundred millions should receive added benefit.

sentences.zh: 可大赦天下。

translations.literal: A general amnesty may be proclaimed for the empire.
translations.idiomatic: A general amnesty is proclaimed for the empire.

sentences.zh: 」壬午，詔曰：「育物惟寬，馭民惟惠，道著興王，本非隸役。

translations.literal: On renwu an edict said: "In nourishing creatures be only broad; in governing the people be only kind—the Way that marks a founding king was never bondage in origin.
translations.idiomatic: On renwu an edict said, "In nurturing things be broad; in governing the people be kind—the Way of founding kings was never meant for servitude.

sentences.zh: 或開奉國，便致擒虜，或在邊疆，濫被抄劫。

translations.literal: Some opened their gates to serve the state and at once were taken captive; some on the frontiers were wantonly plundered in raids.
translations.idiomatic: Some who opened their gates in loyalty were seized at once; some on the borders were wantonly raided.

sentences.zh: 二邦是競，黎元何罪！

translations.literal: Two realms contend—what crime have the common people!
translations.idiomatic: Two states contend—what crime have the common people!

sentences.zh: 朕以寡昧，創承鴻業，旣臨率土，化行宇宙，豈欲使彼獨為匪民。

translations.literal: We, slight and dull, newly inherit the great enterprise; having come to rule all within the four seas and spread transformation through the cosmos, how could we wish them alone to be outlaws?
translations.idiomatic: I, slight and dull, have newly received the great enterprise; now that I rule all within the seas and my transforming influence fills the cosmos, how could I wish them alone to be outcasts?

sentences.zh: 諸州見在北人為奴婢者，並及妻兒，悉可原放。

translations.literal: Northerners now held as slaves and maidservants in the various provinces, together with wives and children, may all be released and forgiven.
translations.idiomatic: Northerners now held as slaves and maidservants in the provinces, with wives and children, may all be released.

sentences.zh: 」癸未，追諡妃王氏為簡皇后。

translations.literal: On guiwei posthumous title was given to Consort Wang as Empress Jian.
translations.idiomatic: On guiwei Consort Wang was posthumously titled Empress Jian.

sentences.zh: 六月丙戌，以南康嗣王會理為司空。

translations.literal: In the sixth month, day bingxu, the Heir of Nankang Prince Huili was made Minister of Works.
translations.idiomatic: On bingxu in the sixth month the heir of Nankang Prince Huili was made Minister of Works.

sentences.zh: 丁亥，立宣城王大器為皇太子。

translations.literal: On dinghai Prince of Xuancheng Daqi was established as crown prince.
translations.idiomatic: On dinghai Prince Daqi of Xuancheng was established as crown prince.

sentences.zh: 壬辰，封當陽公大心為尋陽郡王，石城公大款為江夏郡王，寧國公大臨為南海郡王，臨城公大連為南郡王，西豊公大春為安陸郡王，新塗公大成為山陽郡王，臨湘公大封為宜都郡王。

translations.literal: On renchen Duke of Dangyang Daxin was enfeoffed as Prince of Xunyang commandery, Duke of Shicheng Dakuan as Prince of Jiangxia, Duke of Ningguo Dalin as Prince of Nanhai, Duke of Lincheng Dalian as Prince of Nan commandery, Duke of Xifeng Dachun as Prince of Anlu, Duke of Xintu Dacheng as Prince of Shanyang, Duke of Linxiang Dafeng as Prince of Yidu.
translations.idiomatic: On renchen Duke Daxin of Dangyang became Prince of Xunyang, Duke Dakuan of Shicheng Prince of Jiangxia, Duke Dalin of Ningguo Prince of Nanhai, Duke Dalian of Lincheng Prince of Nan commandery, Duke Dachun of Xifeng Prince of Anlu, Duke Dacheng of Xintu Prince of Shanyang, and Duke Dafeng of Linxiang Prince of Yidu.

sentences.zh: 秋七月甲寅，廣州刺史元景仲謀應侯景，西江督護陳霸先起兵攻之，景仲自殺，霸先迎定州刺史蕭勃為刺史。

translations.literal: In autumn, the seventh month, day jiayin, Guangzhou Inspector Yuan Jingzhong plotted to join Hou Jing; West River Protector Chen Baxian raised troops and attacked him; Jingzhong killed himself and Baxian welcomed Dingzhou Inspector Xiao Bo as inspector.
translations.idiomatic: On jiayin in the seventh month of autumn Guangzhou inspector Yuan Jingzhong plotted to join Hou Jing; West River Protector Chen Baxian rose against him; Jingzhong killed himself and Baxian installed Dingzhou inspector Xiao Bo as inspector.

sentences.zh: 戊辰，以吳郡置吳州，以安陸王大春為刺史。

translations.literal: On wuchen Wu commandery was made into Wu province, with Prince of Anlu Dachun as inspector.
translations.idiomatic: On wuchen Wu commandery was made Wu province, with Prince Dachun of Anlu as inspector.

sentences.zh: 庚午，以司空南康嗣王會理兼尚書令，南海王大臨為揚州刺史，新興王大莊為南徐州刺史。

translations.literal: On gengwu the Heir of Nankang Prince Huili, Minister of Works, additionally became Director of the Masters of Writing; Prince of Nanhai Dalin was made Yangzhou Inspector; Prince of Xinxing Dazhuang was made South Xuzhou Inspector.
translations.idiomatic: On gengwu the heir of Nankang Prince Huili, Minister of Works, also became Director of the Masters of Writing; Prince Dalin of Nanhai became Yangzhou inspector; Prince Dazhuang of Xinxing became South Xuzhou inspector.

sentences.zh: 是月，九江大饑，人相食十四五。

translations.literal: That month in Jiujiang there was great famine; one person in fourteen or fifteen ate another.
translations.idiomatic: That month Jiujiang suffered great famine; one in fourteen or fifteen people ate human flesh.

sentences.zh: 八月癸卯，征東大將軍、開府儀同三司、南徐州刺史蕭淵藻薨。

translations.literal: In the eighth month, day guimao, Grand General Who Conquers the East, Bearer of the Full Staff with honors equal to the Three Lords, and South Xuzhou Inspector Xiao Yuanzao died.
translations.idiomatic: On guimao in the eighth month Grand General Who Conquers the East Xiao Yuanzao, Bearer of the Full Staff, and South Xuzhou inspector, died.

sentences.zh: 冬十月丁未，地震。

translations.literal: In winter, the tenth month, day dingwei, there was an earthquake.
translations.idiomatic: On dingwei in the tenth month of winter there was an earthquake.

sentences.zh: 十二月，百濟國遣使獻方物。

translations.literal: In the twelfth month, Baekje sent envoys presenting tribute goods.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth month Baekje sent envoys with tribute.

sentences.zh: 大寶元年春正月辛亥朔，以國哀不朝會。

translations.literal: On xinhai, the first day of the first month of spring in year 1 of Dabao, because of national mourning there was no court assembly.
translations.idiomatic: On xinhai, the new-year's day of Dabao 1, national mourning prevented the court assembly.

sentences.zh: 詔曰：「蓋天下者，至公之神器，在昔三五，不獲已而臨蒞之。

translations.literal: An edict said: "All under Heaven is the sacred vessel of utmost fairness; in ages past the Three Sovereigns and Five Emperors took the throne only because they had no choice.
translations.idiomatic: An edict said, "All under Heaven is the sacred vessel of utmost fairness; in antiquity the Three Sovereigns and Five Emperors took the throne only when they could not refuse.

sentences.zh: 故帝王之功，聖人之餘事。

translations.literal: Thus the achievement of emperors and kings is what sages leave over.
translations.idiomatic: Thus the work of emperors and kings is what sages leave as surplus.

sentences.zh: 軒冕之華，儻來之一物。

translations.literal: The glory of chariot and cap is something that came by chance.
translations.idiomatic: Chariot and cap are adornments that come by chance alone.

sentences.zh: 太祖文皇帝含光大之量，啓西伯之基。

translations.literal: Grand Ancestor the Literary Emperor embraced a great measure of hidden light and opened the foundation of the Western Earl.
translations.idiomatic: Grand Ancestor the Literary Emperor held vast hidden brilliance and laid the foundation of the Western Earl.

sentences.zh: 高祖武皇帝道洽二儀，智周萬物。

translations.literal: The Martial Emperor, the Gaozu, made the Way pervade the two principles and wisdom compass the myriad things.
translations.idiomatic: Gaozu the Martial Emperor made the Way fill the two principles and his wisdom encompass the myriad things.

sentences.zh: 屬齊季薦瘥，彝倫剝喪，同氣離入苑之禍，元首懷無厭之欲，乃當樂推之運，因億兆之心，承彼掎角，雪茲讎恥。

translations.literal: When the late Qi era brought repeated pestilence and constant norms were stripped away, flesh-and-blood kin suffered the calamity of entering the park, and the ruler harbored insatiable desire—then we met the fortune of the people's willing elevation, drew on the hearts of the hundred millions, received their allied support, and avenged this shame.
translations.idiomatic: When Qi neared its end pestilence returned and moral order collapsed, kin suffered the calamity of the park, and the ruler nursed insatiable desires—then came the fortune of willing elevation, the hearts of the hundred millions were followed, their allied strength was taken up, and this shame was avenged.

sentences.zh: 事非為己，義寔從民。

translations.literal: The affair was not for oneself; in righteousness one truly followed the people.
translations.idiomatic: The deed was not for oneself; in righteousness one truly followed the people.

sentences.zh: 故功成弗居，卑宮菲食，大慈之業普薰，汾陽之詔屢下。

translations.literal: Therefore when achievement was done he did not dwell on it, lived in low halls and plain food, the great compassionate enterprise broadly perfumed, and edicts like those of Fenyang were repeatedly issued.
translations.idiomatic: Therefore when the work was done he did not keep it, dwelt in low halls and ate plain food, great compassion spread widely, and edicts like those of Fenyang were issued again and again.

sentences.zh: 于茲四紀，無得而稱。

translations.literal: For four reign cycles now, none can fully praise it.
translations.idiomatic: For four reign cycles there has been no fully fitting praise.

sentences.zh: 朕以寡昧，哀煢孔棘，生靈已盡，志不圖全，僶俛視陰，企承鴻緒。

translations.literal: We, slight and dull, in deepest grief and distress—the living souls are spent and our will does not plan for wholeness; we bend low and look to shade, hoping to inherit the great thread.
translations.idiomatic: I, slight and dull, am in deepest grief and distress; the living are exhausted and my will does not aim at wholeness; bowing low I await shade and hope to inherit the great succession.

sentences.zh: 懸旌履薄，未足云喻。

translations.literal: Suspended banners over thin ice—words barely suffice.
translations.idiomatic: Banners hang over thin ice—words can scarcely tell it.

sentences.zh: 痛甚愈遲，諒闇彌切。

translations.literal: Pain grows deeper as healing delays; the period of hidden mourning is all the keener.
translations.idiomatic: Pain deepens as recovery is slow; mourning seclusion grows keener still.

sentences.zh: 方當玄默在躬，栖心事外。

translations.literal: We should keep dark silence within and lodge the mind in matters beyond.
translations.idiomatic: I should keep dark silence within and lodge my mind outside affairs.

sentences.zh: 卽王道未直，天步猶艱，式憑宰輔，以弘庶政。

translations.literal: Yet the kingly Way is not yet straight and the heavenly course still hard—we must rely on chief ministers to expand the myriad administrations.
translations.idiomatic: Yet the kingly Way is not yet straight and the heavenly steps still hard; I must rely on chief ministers to broaden the myriad affairs of state.

sentences.zh: 履端建號，仰惟舊章。

translations.literal: Observing the year's beginning, we establish the era name, looking up to the old statutes.
translations.idiomatic: At the year's beginning I establish the era name, looking up to the old statutes.

sentences.zh: 可大赦天下，改太清四年為大寶元年。

translations.literal: A general amnesty may be proclaimed; Taiqing year 4 is changed to Dabao year 1.
translations.idiomatic: A general amnesty is proclaimed and Taiqing 4 is changed to Dabao 1.

sentences.zh: 」丁巳，天雨黃沙。

translations.literal: On dingsi yellow sand rained from the sky.
translations.idiomatic: On dingsi yellow sand fell from the sky.

sentences.zh: 己未，太白經天，辛酉乃止。

translations.literal: On jiwei Venus crossed the sky; on xinyou it ceased.
translations.idiomatic: On jiwei Venus crossed the heavens; on xinyou it stopped.

sentences.zh: 西魏寇安陸，執司州刺史柳仲禮，盡沒漢東之地。

translations.literal: Western Wei raided Anlu, seized Sizhou Inspector Liu Zhongli, and wholly lost the lands east of the Han.
translations.idiomatic: Western Wei raided Anlu, seized Sizhou inspector Liu Zhongli, and took all the lands east of the Han.

sentences.zh: 丙寅，月晝見。

translations.literal: On bingyin the moon was seen in daytime.
translations.idiomatic: On bingyin the moon was visible by day.

sentences.zh: 癸酉，前江都令祖皓起義，襲廣陵，斬賊南兗州刺史董紹先。

translations.literal: On guiyou former Jiangdu magistrate Zu Hao rose in revolt, struck Guangling, and beheaded the rebel South Yanzhou Inspector Dong Shaoxian.
translations.idiomatic: On guiyou former Jiangdu magistrate Zu Hao rose, attacked Guangling, and beheaded the rebel South Yanzhou inspector Dong Shaoxian.

sentences.zh: 侯景自帥水步軍擊皓。

translations.literal: Hou Jing personally led infantry and naval forces to attack Hao.
translations.idiomatic: Hou Jing personally led land and river forces against Hao.

sentences.zh: 二月癸未，景攻陷廣陵，皓等並見害。

translations.literal: In the second month, day guiwei, Jing captured Guangling; Hao and others were all killed.
translations.idiomatic: On guiwei in the second month Hou Jing took Guangling; Hao and the others were all killed.

sentences.zh: 丙戌，以安陸王大春為東揚州刺史。

translations.literal: On bingxu Prince of Anlu Dachun was made East Yangzhou Inspector.
translations.idiomatic: On bingxu Prince Dachun of Anlu was made East Yangzhou inspector.

sentences.zh: 省吳州，如先為郡。

translations.literal: Wu province was abolished and restored as a commandery as before.
translations.idiomatic: Wu province was abolished and Wu was again a commandery as before.

sentences.zh: 詔曰：「近東垂擾亂，江陽縱逸。

translations.literal: An edict said: "Recently the eastern marches were disturbed and Jiangyang ran loose.
translations.idiomatic: An edict said, "Recently the eastern marches were disturbed and Jiangyang ran wild.

sentences.zh: 上宰運謀，猛士雄奮，吳、會肅清，濟、兗澄謐，京師畿內，無事戎衣。

translations.literal: Chief ministers deployed strategy, bold warriors fought fiercely; Wu and Kuaiji were cleared, Ji and Yan were calm, and within the capital region there was no need for martial dress.
translations.idiomatic: Chief ministers deployed strategy and bold warriors fought fiercely; Wu and Kuaiji were cleared, Ji and Yan were calm, and within the capital precincts there was no need for armor.

sentences.zh: 朝廷達宮，齋內左右，並可解嚴。

translations.literal: Court palaces of rank and those left and right within the fasting quarters may all stand down from alert.
translations.idiomatic: Court palaces of rank and the attendants left and right within the fasting quarters may all stand down from alert.

sentences.zh: 」乙巳，以尚書僕射王克為左僕射。

translations.literal: On yisi Vice Director of the Masters of Writing Wang Ke was made Left Vice Director.
translations.idiomatic: On yisi Wang Ke, Vice Director of the Masters of Writing, became Left Vice Director.

sentences.zh: 是月，邵陵王綸自尋陽至于夏口，郢州刺史南平王恪以州讓綸。

translations.literal: That month Prince of Shaoling Lun came from Xunyang to Xiakou; Jingzhou Inspector Prince of Nanping Ke yielded the province to Lun.
translations.idiomatic: That month Prince Lun of Shaoling came from Xunyang to Xiakou; Jingzhou inspector Prince Ke of Nanping yielded the province to him.

sentences.zh: 丙午，侯景逼太宗幸西州。

translations.literal: On bingwu Hou Jing compelled the Taizong to visit Xizhou.
translations.idiomatic: On bingwu Hou Jing forced Taizong to go to Xizhou.

sentences.zh: 夏五月庚午，征北將軍、開府儀同三司鄱陽嗣王範薨。

translations.literal: In summer, the fifth month, day gengwu, General Who Conquers the North, Bearer of the Full Staff, and Heir of Poyang Prince Fan died.
translations.idiomatic: On gengwu in the fifth month of summer General Who Conquers the North and heir of Poyang Prince Fan, Bearer of the Full Staff, died.

sentences.zh: 自春迄夏，大饑，人相食，京師尤甚。

translations.literal: From spring through summer there was great famine; people ate one another, especially in the capital.
translations.idiomatic: From spring through summer famine was severe; people ate one another, especially in the capital.

sentences.zh: 六月辛巳，以南郡王大連行揚州事。

translations.literal: In the sixth month, day xinsi, Prince of Nan commandery Dalian was assigned to handle Yangzhou affairs.
translations.idiomatic: On xinsi in the sixth month Prince Dalian of Nan commandery was put in charge of Yangzhou affairs.

sentences.zh: 庚子，前司州刺史羊鴉仁自尚書省出奔西州。

translations.literal: On gengzi former Sizhou Inspector Yang Yaren fled from the Masters of Writing office to Xizhou.
translations.idiomatic: On gengzi former Sizhou inspector Yang Yaren fled from the Masters of Writing to Xizhou.

sentences.zh: 秋七月戊辰，賊行臺任約寇江州，刺史尋陽王大心以州降約。

translations.literal: In autumn, the seventh month, day wuchen, the rebel Mobile Headquarters Ren Yue raided Jiangzhou; Inspector Prince of Xunyang Daxin surrendered the province to Yue.
translations.idiomatic: On wuchen in the seventh month of autumn the rebel Mobile Headquarters Ren Yue raided Jiangzhou; inspector Prince Daxin of Xunyang surrendered the province to him.

sentences.zh: 是月，以南郡王大連為江州刺史。

translations.literal: That month Prince of Nan commandery Dalian was made Jiangzhou Inspector.
translations.idiomatic: That month Prince Dalian of Nan commandery was made Jiangzhou inspector.

sentences.zh: 八月甲午，湘東王繹遣領軍將軍王僧辯率衆逼郢州。

translations.literal: In the eighth month, day jiawu, Prince of Xiangdong Yi sent Army Inspector General Wang Sengbian leading the host to press Yingzhou.
translations.idiomatic: On jiawu in the eighth month Prince Yi of Xiangdong sent Army Inspector General Wang Senbian with troops to press Yingzhou.

sentences.zh: 乙亥，侯景自進位相國，封二十郡為漢王。

translations.literal: On yihai Hou Jing advanced himself to Chancellor of State and enfeoffed over twenty commanderies as King of Han.
translations.idiomatic: On yihai Hou Jing made himself Chancellor of State and enfeoffed twenty commanderies as King of Han.

sentences.zh: 邵陵王綸棄郢州走。

translations.literal: Prince of Shaoling Lun abandoned Yingzhou and fled.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Lun of Shaoling abandoned Yingzhou and fled.

sentences.zh: 冬十月乙未，侯景又逼太宗幸西州曲宴，自加宇宙大將軍、都督六合諸軍事。

translations.literal: In winter, the tenth month, day yiwei, Hou Jing again compelled the Taizong to attend a banquet at Xizhou, and himself added Grand General of the Cosmos and Commander over military affairs in the Six Harmonized Directions.
translations.idiomatic: On yiwei in the tenth month of winter Hou Jing again forced Taizong to a banquet at Xizhou and made himself Grand General of the Cosmos and commander of the Six Harmonized Directions.

sentences.zh: 立皇子大鈞為西陽郡王，大威為武寧郡王，大球為建安郡王，大昕為義安郡王，大摯為綏建郡王，大圜為樂梁郡王。

translations.literal: Imperial sons Dagun, Dawei, Daqiu, Daxin, Dazhi, and Dayuan were enfeoffed as princes of Xiyang, Wuning, Jian'an, Yi'an, Suijian, and Yuele commanderies.
translations.idiomatic: The princes Dagun, Dawei, Daqiu, Daxin, Dazhi, and Dayuan were enfeoffed as princes of Xiyang, Wuning, Jian'an, Yi'an, Suijian, and Yuele commanderies.

sentences.zh: 壬寅，景害南康嗣王會理。

translations.literal: On renyin Jing killed the Heir of Nankang Prince Huili.
translations.idiomatic: On renyin Hou Jing killed the heir of Nankang Prince Huili.

sentences.zh: 十一月，任約進據西陽，分兵寇齊昌，執衡陽王獻送京師，害之。

translations.literal: In the eleventh month Ren Yue advanced and held Xiyang, sent detached troops to raid Qichang, seized Prince of Hengyang Xian and sent him to the capital, then killed him.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh month Ren Yue advanced and held Xiyang, detached troops to raid Qichang, seized Prince Xian of Hengyang and sent him to the capital, then killed him.

sentences.zh: 湘東王繹遣前寧州刺史徐文盛督衆軍拒約。

translations.literal: Prince of Xiangdong Yi sent former Ningzhou Inspector Xu Wensheng to command the armies against Yue.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Yi of Xiangdong sent former Ningzhou inspector Xu Wensheng to command the armies against Yue.

sentences.zh: 南郡王前中兵張彪起義於會稽若邪山，攻破浙東諸縣。

translations.literal: Former Central Army officer of the Prince of Nan commandery Zhang Biao rose at Ruoye Mountain in Kuaiji and broke through the counties of eastern Zhejiang.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Biao, former central army officer of the Prince of Nan commandery, rose on Ruoye Mountain in Kuaiji and overran the counties of eastern Zhejiang.

sentences.zh: 二年春二月，邵陵王綸走至安陸董城，為西魏所攻，軍敗，死。

translations.literal: In the second month of spring, year 2, Prince of Shaoling Lun fled to Dongcheng in Anlu, was attacked by Western Wei, his army was defeated, and he died.
translations.idiomatic: In the second month of spring, year 2, Prince Lun of Shaoling fled to Dongcheng in Anlu, was attacked by Western Wei, was defeated, and died.

sentences.zh: 三月，侯景自帥衆西寇。

translations.literal: In the third month Hou Jing personally led his host westward on campaign.
translations.idiomatic: In the third month Hou Jing personally led his army west on campaign.

sentences.zh: 丁未，發京師，自石頭至新林，舳艫相接。

translations.literal: On dingwei, he set out from the capital; from Shitou to Xinlin, war vessels linked stem to stern.
translations.idiomatic: On dingwei day he marched from the capital; from Shitou to Xinlin, boats stretched bow to stern without a break.

sentences.zh: 四月，至西陽。

translations.literal: In the fourth month, he reached Xiyang.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth month he reached Xiyang.

sentences.zh: 乙亥，景分遣偽將宋子仙、任約襲郢州。

translations.literal: On yihai, Jing sent out in detachments the rebel generals Song Zixian and Ren Yue to raid Yingzhou.
translations.idiomatic: On yihai day Hou Jing detached the rebel generals Song Zixian and Ren Yue to strike Yingzhou.

sentences.zh: 丙子，執刺史蕭方諸。

translations.literal: On bingzi, they seized Inspector Xiao Fangzhu.
translations.idiomatic: On bingzi day they seized inspector Xiao Fangzhu.

sentences.zh: 閏月甲子，景進寇巴陵，湘東王繹所遣領軍將軍王僧辯連戰不能剋。

translations.literal: In the intercalary month, day jiazi, Jing advanced to attack Baling; Wang Senbian, commanding general sent by Prince Yi of Xiangdong, fought repeatedly but could not overcome him.
translations.idiomatic: On jiazi in the intercalary month Hou Jing pressed on Baling; Wang Senbian, the commanding general Prince Yi of Xiangdong had sent, fought again and again but could not win.

sentences.zh: 五月癸未，湘東王驛遣遊擊將軍胡僧祐、信州刺史陸法和援巴陵，景遣任約帥衆拒援軍。

translations.literal: On guwei, fifth month, Prince Yi of Xiangdong urgently sent Mobile Corps General Hu Sengyou and Xin province Inspector Lu Fahe to relieve Baling; Jing sent Ren Yue to lead troops to resist the relief army.
translations.idiomatic: On guwei in the fifth month Prince Yi of Xiangdong urgently sent mobile corps general Hu Sengyou and Xin province inspector Lu Fahe to relieve Baling; Hou Jing sent Ren Yue with an army to block them.

sentences.zh: 六月甲辰，僧祐等擊破任約，擒之。

translations.literal: On jiachen, sixth month, Sengyou and others defeated and captured Ren Yue.
translations.idiomatic: On jiachen in the sixth month Sengyou and his forces routed Ren Yue and took him prisoner.

sentences.zh: 乙巳，景解圍宵遁，王僧辯督衆軍追景。

translations.literal: On yisi, Jing lifted the siege and fled by night; Wang Senbian directed the massed armies in pursuit of Jing.
translations.idiomatic: On yisi day Hou Jing broke the siege and fled under cover of night; Wang Senbian led the combined armies in pursuit.

sentences.zh: 庚申，攻魯山城，剋之，獲魏司徒張化仁、儀同門洪慶。

translations.literal: On gengshen, they attacked Lushan fortress, took it, and captured Wei Minister of Education Zhang Huaren and Formation Companion Men Hongqing.
translations.idiomatic: On gengshen day they stormed Lushan fortress, took it, and captured Wei minister of education Zhang Huaren and formation companion Men Hongqing.

sentences.zh: 辛酉，進圍郢州，下之，獲賊帥宋子仙等。

translations.literal: On xinyou, they advanced to besiege Yingzhou, took it, and captured the rebel leaders Song Zixian and others.
translations.idiomatic: On xinyou day they pressed the siege of Yingzhou, took the city, and captured the rebel chiefs Song Zixian and others.

sentences.zh: 鄱陽王故將侯瑱起兵，襲偽儀同于慶于豫章，慶敗走。

translations.literal: A former general of the Prince of Poyang, Hou Zhen, raised troops and attacked the false Formation Companion Yu Qing at Yuzhang; Qing was defeated and fled.
translations.idiomatic: Hou Zhen, a former officer of the Prince of Poyang, raised troops and struck the rebel formation companion Yu Qing at Yuzhang; Qing was beaten and fled.

sentences.zh: 秋七月丁亥，侯景還至京師。

translations.literal: In the seventh month of autumn, day dinghai, Hou Jing returned to the capital.
translations.idiomatic: On dinghai day in the seventh month of autumn Hou Jing returned to the capital.

sentences.zh: 辛丑，王僧辯軍次湓城，賊行江州事范希榮棄城走。

translations.literal: On xinchou, Wang Senbian's army halted at Pencheng; Fan Xirong, who held Jiangzhou affairs for the rebels, abandoned the city and fled.
translations.idiomatic: On xinchou day Wang Senbian's army camped at Pencheng; Fan Xirong, the rebel officer in charge of Jiangzhou, abandoned the city and fled.

sentences.zh: 八月丙午，晉熙人王僧振、鄭寵起兵襲郡城，偽晉州刺史夏侯威生、儀同任延遁走。

translations.literal: On bingwu, eighth month, Wang Sengzhen and Zheng Chong of Jinxi raised troops and raided the commandery seat; the false Jinzhou Inspector Xia Hou Weisheng and Formation Companion Ren Yan fled.
translations.idiomatic: On bingwu in the eighth month Wang Sengzhen and Zheng Chong of Jinxi rose and stormed the commandery seat; the rebel Jinzhou inspector Xia Hou Weisheng and formation companion Ren Yan fled.

sentences.zh: 戊午，侯景遣衛尉卿彭俊、廂公王僧貴率兵入殿，廢太宗為晉安王，幽于永福省。

translations.literal: On wuwu, Hou Jing sent Minister of the Guard Peng Jun and Palace Section Commander Wang Senggui to lead troops into the hall, deposed Taizong as Prince of Jin'an, and confined him in Yongfu Palace.
translations.idiomatic: On wuwu day Hou Jing sent minister of the guard Peng Jun and palace section commander Wang Senggui with troops into the hall, deposed Taizong as Prince of Jin'an, and imprisoned him in Yongfu Palace.

sentences.zh: 害皇太子大器、尋陽王大心、西陽王大鈞、武寧王大威、建平王大球、義安王大昕及尋陽王諸子二十人。

translations.literal: He killed Crown Prince Daqi, Prince of Xunyang Daxin, Prince of Xiyang Dajun, Prince of Wuning Dawei, Prince of Jianping Daqiu, Prince of Yi'an Daxin, and twenty sons of the Prince of Xunyang.
translations.idiomatic: He killed Crown Prince Daqi, the princes of Xunyang, Xiyang, Wuning, Jianping, and Yi'an, and twenty sons of the Prince of Xunyang.

sentences.zh: 矯為太宗詔，禪于豫章嗣王棟，大赦改年。

translations.literal: Forging an edict in Taizong's name, he abdicated to the Successor Prince of Yuzhang, Dong; a general amnesty was proclaimed and the reign title changed.
translations.idiomatic: He forged an abdication edict in Taizong's name to the successor prince of Yuzhang, Dong, proclaimed a general amnesty, and changed the reign title.

sentences.zh: 遣使害南海王大臨于吳郡，南郡王大連于姑孰，安陸王大春於會稽，新興王大莊於京口。

translations.literal: Envoys were sent to kill Prince of Nanhai Dailin at Wu commandery, Prince of Nanjun Dalian at Gudu, Prince of Anlu Dachun at Kuaiji, and Prince of Xinxing Dazhuang at Jingkou.
translations.idiomatic: Envoys were sent to kill Prince Dailin of Nanhai at Wu, Prince Dalian of Nanjun at Gudu, Prince Dachun of Anlu at Kuaiji, and Prince Dazhuang of Xinxing at Jingkou.

sentences.zh: 冬十月壬寅，帝謂舍人殷不害曰：「吾昨夜夢吞土，卿試為我思之。

translations.literal: In the tenth month of winter, day renyin, the Emperor said to Attendant Yin Buhai: "Last night I dreamed I swallowed earth—try to interpret it for me.
translations.idiomatic: On renyin in the tenth month of winter the emperor said to attendant Yin Buhai, "Last night I dreamed I swallowed earth—please interpret it for me.

sentences.zh: 」不害曰：「昔重耳饋塊，卒還晉國。

translations.literal: " Buhai said: "In old times Chong'er was given a clod of earth and at last returned to the state of Jin.
translations.idiomatic: " Buhai said, "Long ago Chong'er was given a clod of earth and at last returned to Jin.

sentences.zh: 陛下所夢，得符是乎。

translations.literal: What Your Majesty dreamed accords with that, does it not?"
translations.idiomatic: Surely Your Majesty's dream matches that sign?"

sentences.zh: 」及王偉等進觴於帝曰：「丞相以陛下憂憤旣久，使臣上壽。

translations.literal: When Wang Wei and the others came forward with a toast to the Emperor, they said: "The Chancellor, seeing Your Majesty's long grief and distress, has sent us to offer longevity wine."
translations.idiomatic: Then Wang Wei and the others came forward with a toast and said, "The chancellor, seeing Your Majesty's long grief, has sent us to offer longevity wine."

sentences.zh: 」帝笑曰：「壽酒，不得盡此乎？

translations.literal: The Emperor smiled and said: "Longevity wine—must it not be drunk to the end?"
translations.idiomatic: The emperor smiled and said, "Longevity wine—must it not be drunk to the dregs?"

sentences.zh: 」於是並賚酒肴、曲項琵琶，與帝飲。

translations.literal: Thereupon they all bestowed wine and food, a curved-neck pipa, and drank with the Emperor.
translations.idiomatic: They then gave wine and food, a curved-neck pipa, and drank with him.

sentences.zh: 帝知不免，乃盡酣，曰：「不圖為樂一至於斯！

translations.literal: Knowing he could not escape, the Emperor drank his fill and said: "I never thought pleasure could reach this point!"
translations.idiomatic: Knowing he could not escape, the emperor drank his fill and said, "I never thought merriment could come to this!"

sentences.zh: 」旣醉寢，王偉、彭儁進土囊，王修纂坐其上，於是太宗崩於永福省，時年四十九。

translations.literal: When he was drunk and asleep, Wang Wei and Peng Jun brought in a bag of earth; Wang Xiuzuan sat upon it—and thereupon Taizong died in Yongfu Palace, aged forty-nine.
translations.idiomatic: When he was drunk and asleep, Wang Wei and Peng Jun brought in a bag of earth; Wang Xiuzuan sat on it—and Taizong died in Yongfu Palace at the age of forty-nine.

sentences.zh: 賊偽諡曰明皇帝，廟稱高宗。

translations.literal: The rebels gave the posthumous title Bright Emperor and the temple name Gaozong.
translations.idiomatic: The rebels gave him the posthumous title Bright Emperor and the temple name Gaozong.

sentences.zh: 明年，三月己丑，王僧辯率前百官奉梓宮升朝堂，世祖追崇為簡文皇帝，廟曰太宗。

translations.literal: The next year, third month, day jichou, Wang Senbian led the former hundred officials in escorting the coffin up the audience hall; Shizu posthumously honored him as Emperor Jianwen, with temple name Taizong.
translations.idiomatic: The next year, on jichou in the third month, Wang Senbian led the former hundred officials to raise the coffin to the audience hall; Shizu posthumously honored him as Emperor Jianwen with temple name Taizong.

sentences.zh: 四月乙丑，葬莊陵。

translations.literal: Fourth month, day yichou, he was buried at Zhuang Mausoleum.
translations.idiomatic: On yichou in the fourth month he was buried at Zhuang Mausoleum.

sentences.zh: 初，太宗見幽縶，題壁自序云：「有梁正士蘭陵蕭世纘，立身行道，終始如一，風雨如晦，雞鳴不已。

translations.literal: At first, when Taizong was imprisoned, he wrote a self-account on the wall, saying: "I, Xiao Shizuan of Lanling, upright man of Liang, in conduct from first to last one—though wind and rain darken the sky, the cock crows without cease.
translations.idiomatic: At first, when Taizong was held captive, he wrote on the wall: "I, Xiao Shizuan of Lanling, upright man of Liang, one in conduct from start to finish—though wind and rain darken the sky, the cock crows without cease.

sentences.zh: 弗欺暗室，豈況三光，數至於此，命也如何！

translations.literal: I would not deceive a dark room—how much less the three luminaries; to reach this number is fate—what can be done!"
translations.idiomatic: I would not deceive a dark room—how much less the sun, moon, and stars; to come to this count is fate—what can be done!"

sentences.zh: 」又為《連珠》二首，文甚悽愴。

translations.literal: He also composed two Linked Pearls pieces, the text deeply mournful.
translations.idiomatic: He also wrote two "Linked Pearls" pieces, their tone deeply mournful.

sentences.zh: 太宗幼而敏睿，識悟過人，六歲便屬文，高祖驚其早就，弗之信也。

translations.literal: Taizong from youth was keen and perceptive, his understanding surpassing others; at six he could compose texts, and Gaozu marveled at his early maturity but did not believe it.
translations.idiomatic: Taizong from childhood was quick and perceptive, his insight beyond others; at six he could write, and Gaozu marveled at his early gift but did not believe it.

sentences.zh: 乃於御前面試，辭采甚美。

translations.literal: He was then tested before the imperial presence, and his literary color was very fine.
translations.idiomatic: He was tested before the throne, and his literary grace was superb.

sentences.zh: 高祖歎曰：「此子，吾家之東阿。

translations.literal: Gaozu sighed and said: "This boy is our family's Dong'e."
translations.idiomatic: Gaozu sighed and said, "This boy is our family's Dong'e."

sentences.zh: 」旣長，器宇寬弘，未嘗見慍喜。

translations.literal: When he grew up, his bearing was broad and magnanimous; he was never seen angry or pleased.
translations.idiomatic: When he grew up, his bearing was broad and calm; anger and delight never showed on his face.

sentences.zh: 方頰豊下，須鬢如畫，眄睞則目光燭人。

translations.literal: Square of cheek and full below, his beard and temples like a painting; when he glanced sidelong his gaze lit upon men.
translations.idiomatic: Square of cheek and full below, beard and temples like painted lines; a sidelong glance lit upon men like fire.

sentences.zh: 讀書十行俱下。

translations.literal: In reading he took in ten lines at once.
translations.idiomatic: In reading he took in ten lines at a glance.

sentences.zh: 九流百氏，經目必記；

translations.literal: Of the nine schools and the hundred clans, what passed his eye he always remembered;
translations.idiomatic: Of the nine schools and hundred thinkers, whatever passed his eye he remembered;

sentences.zh: 篇章辭賦，操筆立成。

translations.literal: in essays, rhapsodies, and verse he took up the brush and finished at once.
translations.idiomatic: in essays, rhapsodies, and verse he took up the brush and finished on the spot.

sentences.zh: 博綜儒書，善言玄理。

translations.literal: Broadly versed in Confucian books, skilled in discoursing on Dark Learning.
translations.idiomatic: He mastered Confucian classics and was skilled in Neo-Daoist discourse.

sentences.zh: 自年十一，便能親庶務，歷試蕃政，所在有稱。

translations.literal: From age eleven he could personally attend to the multitude of affairs; repeatedly tested in frontier administration, wherever he went he won praise.
translations.idiomatic: From age eleven he could handle routine affairs himself; repeatedly tried in frontier posts, wherever he went he won praise.

sentences.zh: 在穆貴嬪憂，哀毀骨立，晝夜號泣不絕聲，所坐之席，沾濕盡爛。

translations.literal: In mourning for Noble Consort Mu, his grief wasted him to bone; day and night his weeping never ceased, and the mat he sat on was soaked through and rotted.
translations.idiomatic: Mourning Noble Consort Mu, grief wasted him to bone; day and night he wept without pause, and the mat he sat on rotted from wetting.

sentences.zh: 在襄陽拜表北伐，遣長史柳津、司馬董當門，壯武將軍杜懷寶、振遠將軍曹義宗等衆軍進討，剋平南陽、新野等郡，魏南荊州刺史李志據安昌城降，拓地千餘里。

translations.literal: At Xiangyang he memorialized for a northern campaign; he sent Chief Clerk Liu Jin, Marshal Dong Dangmen, Martial Valor General Du Huaibao, Far-Shaking General Cao Yizong, and others with the massed armies on expedition, conquering Nanyang, Xinye, and other commanderies; Wei's South Jingzhou Inspector Li Zhi, holding Anchang fortress, surrendered, and territory was extended more than a thousand li.
translations.idiomatic: At Xiangyang he memorialized for a northern campaign and sent chief clerk Liu Jin, marshal Dong Dangmen, martial valor general Du Huaibao, far-shaking general Cao Yizong, and others with the armies; they took Nanyang, Xinye, and other commanderies, Wei's south Jingzhou inspector Li Zhi surrendered Anchang fortress, and territory expanded more than a thousand li.

sentences.zh: 及居監撫，多所弘宥，文案簿領，纖毫不可欺。

translations.literal: When he held the regency he was broadly indulgent in many matters, yet in documents and ledgers not the finest thread could be deceived.
translations.idiomatic: As regent he was broadly lenient in many matters, yet in documents and ledgers not the finest thread could be falsified.

sentences.zh: 引納文學之士，賞接無倦，恒討論篇籍，繼以文章。

translations.literal: He drew in men of letters and rewarded them without weariness, constantly discussing texts and following with compositions.
translations.idiomatic: He welcomed literary men and rewarded them tirelessly, constantly discussing texts and then writing himself.

sentences.zh: 高祖所制《五經講疏》，嘗於玄圃奉述，聽者傾朝野。

translations.literal: When Gaozu composed Expositions on the Five Classics, Taizong once presented them at the Dark Garden; listeners filled court and countryside.
translations.idiomatic: When Gaozu composed his Expositions on the Five Classics, Taizong once lectured on them at the Dark Garden; listeners filled court and countryside.

sentences.zh: 雅好題詩，其序云：「余七歲有詩癖，長而不倦。

translations.literal: He loved composing poetry by nature; in his preface he wrote: "At seven I had a poetry mania, and in growing up I never tired of it."
translations.idiomatic: He loved poetry by nature; in his preface he wrote, "At seven I had a poetry mania, and as I grew I never tired of it."

sentences.zh: 」然傷於輕豔，當時號曰「宮體」。

translations.literal: Yet he was faulted for frivolous ornament, and his age styled this the "Palace Style."
translations.idiomatic: Yet he was faulted for frivolous ornament, and his age called it the "Palace Style."

sentences.zh: 所著《昭明太子傳》五卷，《諸王傳》三十卷，《禮大義》二十卷，《老子義》二十卷，《莊子義》二十卷，《長春義記》一百卷，《法寶連璧》三百卷，並行於世焉。

translations.literal: His works included Biography of the Heir Apparent Zhaoming in five scrolls, Biographies of the Princes in thirty scrolls, Great Meaning of the Rites in twenty scrolls, Meaning of the Laozi in twenty scrolls, Meaning of the Zhuangzi in twenty scrolls, Recorded Meaning of Eternal Spring in one hundred scrolls, and Treasured Laws Linked Pearls in three hundred scrolls—all circulated in his time.
translations.idiomatic: His works included Biography of the Heir Apparent Zhaoming in five scrolls, Biographies of the Princes in thirty scrolls, Great Meaning of the Rites in twenty scrolls, Meaning of the Laozi in twenty scrolls, Meaning of the Zhuangzi in twenty scrolls, Recorded Meaning of Eternal Spring in one hundred scrolls, and Treasured Laws Linked Pearls in three hundred scrolls—all circulated in his day.

sentences.zh: 史臣曰：太宗幼年聰睿，令問夙標，天才縱逸，冠於今古。

translations.literal: The historian writes: In youth Taizong was clever and perceptive, his fair renown marked from of old, his heavenly talent unrestrained, foremost in past and present.
translations.idiomatic: The historian writes: In youth Taizong was clever and perceptive, his fair renown marked from of old, his heavenly talent unrestrained, foremost in past and present.

sentences.zh: 文則時以輕華為累，君子所不取焉。

translations.literal: In literature he was at times burdened by frivolous ornament—what gentlemen do not take up.
translations.idiomatic: In literature he was at times burdened by frivolous ornament—what gentlemen do not take up.

sentences.zh: 及養德東朝，聲被夷夏，洎乎繼統，寔有人君之懿矣。

translations.literal: When he cultivated virtue in the Eastern Palace, his fame reached barbarians and Chinese alike; when he succeeded to the throne, he truly had a ruler's excellence.
translations.idiomatic: When he cultivated virtue in the Eastern Palace, his fame reached barbarians and Chinese alike; when he succeeded to the throne, he truly had a ruler's excellence.

sentences.zh: 方符文、景，運鐘《屯》、《剝》，受制賊臣，弗展所蘊，終罹懷、愍之酷，哀哉！

translations.literal: Just as he was to match Wen and Jing, fate struck the hexagrams Tun and Bo; constrained by the rebel minister, he could not unfold what he held within, and at last suffered the cruelty of Huai and Min—alas!
translations.idiomatic: Just as he was to match Wen and Jing, fate struck the hexagrams Tun and Bo; constrained by the rebel minister, he could not unfold what he held within, and at last suffered the cruelty of Huai and Min—alas!

sentences.zh: 全文以中華書局、一九七三年五月版《梁書》爲本校。

translations.literal: The full text was collated against the Zhonghua Shuju edition of the Book of Liang (May 1973).
translations.idiomatic: The full text was collated against the Zhonghua Shuju edition of the Book of Liang (May 1973).
